The case of the prosecution is that on 24.01.2008 at unknown time at unknown place the accused persons in furtherance of their common intention induced the complainant to enter into an agreement for purchase of property bearing no. B-89 Malviya Nagar, New Delhi-17 and to part with a sum of Rs. 4,50,000/- as earnest money which was paid to the accused Madhu Bhatti despite the fact that accused Madhu Bhatti was not the owner of the said property at the relevant time and litigation qua the property in question was pending in the Court and thus the accused persons cheated the complainant and thereby committed offence punishable u/s 420/34 IPC.
PROCEEDINGS BEFORE THE COURT 02.
Upon completion of investigation, charge-sheet for offence punishable under Section 420/34 IPC was filed by the IO.
The cognizance of the offence was taken by the Court and the copy of charge-sheet was supplied to the accused.
Thereafter, charge for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420/34 of IPC was framed upon the accused persons on 28.01.2017 to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

Thereafter, prosecution witnesses were examined,
cross-examined and discharged.
Statement of accused persons u/s 313 Cr.PC was recorded on 09.10.2025

REASONS FOR DECISION 03.

In order to prove the case of prosecution, prosecution examined PW-1 Mukesh Talreja, PW-2 Vipin Kapoor, PW-3 Rajender Gupta, PW-4 Inspector Madhav Singh, PW-5 Retd. SI Vijay Singh and PW-6 Anil Kumar.

04. PW1 Mukesh Talreja in his examination in chief stated that on 24.01.2008 he purchased a property bearing no. B-89, Second Floor, Front Side, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi through one broker namely Kishan Monga from accused Madhu Bhatti and Kishan Monga told PW1 that there was no property dispute relating to the alleged property and Kishan Monga insisted PW1 for giving token State vs Madhu Bhatti Anr on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5881372/
2 money of Rs. 4.5 lakh cash to accused Madhu Bhatti and Shyam Malik.

PW1 further stated that thereafter one sale agreement was executed between him and accused Madhu Bhatti and thereafter he had given Rs. 4.5 lakh in cash to accused persons in the presence of Krishan Kumar Monga.
PW1 further stated that the accused persons assured him that the aforesaid property was free from all the encumbrances at the time of execution of the aforesaid agreement.
Thereafter PW1 asked the accused persons to show the original documents pertaining to the property and at that time accused persons told PW1 to contact their advocate.
PW1 contacted the lawyer of the accused and thereafter the lawyer provided the documents of civil suit between Rupa Tower and accused persons.
PW1 further stated that he got verified the aforesaid documents from his lawyer and his lawyer suggested him that he cannot purchase the property as the civil suit was pending before the Court.
PW1 contacted both accused persons and told them that he is not interested to FIR No. 617/2008 State Vs. Madhu Bhatti Anr. 3 of 6 BHANU PRATAP SINGH PRATAP Date:

PW1 further stated that he waited till 03-04 months but accused persons did not return his money.

05. Perusal of the above testimony of PW1 shows that PW1 refused to purchase the property of the accused Madhu Bhatti on the ground that the civil suit was pending between Rupa Tower and accused Madhu Bhatti.
PW1 in his testimony has only stated regarding the pendency of the civil suit between Rupa Tower and accused Madhu Bhatti regarding the property in question.
PW1 in his testimony has not brought any evidence on record to show that accused Madhu Bhatti was not the owner of the property in question.

This Court is of the view that pendency of civil suit between Rupa Tower and accused Madhu Bhatti is not sufficient to prove that accused Madhu Bhatti was not the owner of the property bearing no. B-89, Second Floor, Malviya Nagar.
Further PW1 has not produced any evidence to show any deception or dishonest inducement by the accused persons regarding property bearing no. B-89, Second Floor, Malviya Nagar.

06. PW3 Rajender Gupta stated in his examination in chief that he is Director M/S Rupa Tower Private Limited and Rupa Tower had filed a suit in Hon'ble High Court of Delhi against Mr. K.L. Malik for specific performance of agreement to sell executed between Rupa Tower and Mr. K.L Malik with regard to property bearing no. B-89,
Malviya Nagar.

PW3 further stated that during the pendency of the above suit, Mr.
Malik agreed to buy one flat in the building in the name of his daughter Ms. Madhu Bhatti.
PW3 further stated that the possession of the said flat was handed over to Madhu Bhatti.

PW3 Rajender Gupta in his cross-examination stated that the Second Floor,
Front Portion of B-89, Malviya Nagar is under the ownership of accused Madhu Bhatti and she is the owner of that very portion.

Further PW3 Rajender Gupta in his 161 CrPC statement has stated that he was not claiming the ownership of the flat at Second Floor, B-89, Malviya Nagar and the possession of the flat has been given to Madhu Bhatti.

08. Perusal of the above testimony of PW3 shows that PW3 Rajender Gupta has not disputed the ownership of accused Madhu Bhatti with respect to Second Floor, Front Portion of B-89, Malviya Nagar in the civil suit pending between Rupa Tower and accused persons.
Therefore, it is evident that PW3 has deposed in favour of the accused persons and PW3 has not supported the case of the prosecution.
09. PW2 Vipin Kumar in his cross-examination stated that he cannot admit or deny the suggestion whether the accused Madhu Bhatti was the owner of B-89, Second Floor, Malviya Nagar.

PW6 Anil Kumar (Deputy Director, Higher Education,
Government of Delhi) stated in his testimony that in the year 2010 he was posted as Sub Registrar-05 at the Office of Sub Registrar, Mehrauli, Delhi.

PW5 in his cross-examination stated that a Sub Registrar is not supposed to say that the documents mentioned in verification letter dated 12.03.2010 Ex.PW6/A in any way can prove or cannot prove the ownership of title of the accused persons in the property no. B-89, Second Floor, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi.
Perusal of testimony of PW2 and PW5 shows that the testimony of both the witnesses does not incriminate the accused persons.
FIR No. 617/2008 State Vs. Madhu Bhatti Anr. 5 of 6 BHANU by BHANU PRATAP SINGH PRATAP 2026.03.27

sentences.text:
Perusal of the testimony of PW4 Inspector Madhav Singh and PW5 SI Vijay Singh shows that they have not brought any document on record to dispute the ownership of accused Madhu Bhatti with respect to property bearing no. B-89, Second Floor,
Front Portion, Malviya Nagar.
Further PW4 and PW5 did not place any evidence on record to show any deception or dishonest inducement by the accused persons regarding property bearing no. B-89, Second Floor, Malviya Nagar.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the testimony of PW4 and PW5 is not sufficient to prove the case of the prosecution.

CONCLUSION:
11. In view of the above reasons, this Court has arrived to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the present case beyond reasonable doubt.

Accordingly, accused persons Madhu Bhatti and Shyam Malik are not guilty in the State vs Madhu Bhatti Anr on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5881372/
4 present case.
Therefore, accused persons Madhu Bhatti and Shyam Malik stand acquitted for the offence under Section 420/34 IPC.
